Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) where possible. - Change passwords regularly and avoid reusing them across different platforms. 2. **Email Security:** - Be cautious of unsolicited emails, especially those requesting personal or financial information. - Verify the sender's identity before clicking on links or downloading attachments. - Report any suspicious emails to the IT department immediately. 3. **Data Handling:** - Encrypt sensitive data both in transit and at rest. - Avoid sharing confidential information over unsecured channels. - Regularly back up important data to prevent loss in case of an attack. 4. **Device Security:** - Keep all devices and software up to date with the latest security patches. - Use antivirus software and enable firewall protections. - Disconnect devices from the network when not in use. 5. **Training and Awareness:** - Participate in regular cybersecurity training sessions. - Stay informed about the latest security best practices and threats. - Encourage colleagues to follow security guidelines and report any concerns. --- **Technical Details for the IT Department** - **Advanced Security Configurations:** - **Access Control:** - Review and update access control policies to enforce the principle of least privilege. - Conduct regular audits of user permissions and access logs. - **Incident Response Plan:** -
